### Observed differences

- Five activities swapped between absent and universal: in the earlier window, A14, A17, A18, A19 and A20 each ran in a minority of traces (about 14–27 in 100, together covering every trace) while A15, A16, A25, A26 and A27 were not observed at all; in the later window the reverse holds — none of the old five appears (0 of 200 traces) and each of the new five occurs exactly once in every trace (200 of 200). [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC002, OCC003, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]

- In the earlier window, the five old activities were strict alternatives — no trace contained two of them — and each case ran A43, then exactly one of the five, then A28, with each of the five leading only onward to A28. [REL003, REL029, REL044, DIR011, DIR001, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL035, REL036]

- In the later window, each of the five new activities always runs after A43 and before A28. [REL018, REL019, REL027, REL028, REL053, REL054, REL056, REL057, REL058, REL059]

- In the later window, the five new activities have no fixed order between them: in all ten of their pairs, either order occurs in roughly half of the traces (shares between about 0.44 and 0.60 in each direction; A15 precedes A16 in about 52 in 100 traces). [REL010, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL051, REL052, REL055]

- A43's observed outgoing transitions moved entirely from the old five (per-successor shares about 0.14–0.27) to the new five (about 0.17–0.25), and each new activity in turn leads to the other four block members and to A28 (per-successor shares about 0.13–0.27). [DIR011, DIR002, DIR003, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010]

- A28 now sits later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.39, up from about 0.39 → 0.47) and A43 earlier (about 0.32 → 0.29), while the new block occupies roughly the same relative region (about 0.37–0.38) that the single old activity occupied (about 0.35–0.37). [POS011, POS012, POS001, POS002, POS005, POS008]

- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A44 and A45 fell from a mean of about 1.0 hour to about 0.5 hour (median about 1.02 → 0.50 hours), on a similar number of observed gaps (157 vs 148). [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A43 and A28 was restructured from a choice into a full pass: in the earlier window each case executed A43, then exactly one of the five alternatives A14, A17, A18, A19 or A20, then A28, whereas in the later window cases execute A43, then all five of A15, A16, A25, A26 and A27 — each exactly once and in no fixed order between them — and then A28. The occurrence, routing and relation indicators all reflect the same underlying difference: both activity sets switch between 0 and 200 of 200 traces; A43's outgoing transitions move wholly from the old set to the new set; the old set is mutually exclusive while the new set co-occurs universally with roughly even mixed pairwise orders; and A43 shifts earlier while A28 shifts later, as expected when the block between them grows from one activity to five. With 92 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.7 expected if nothing had changed, sampling fluctuation cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC002, OCC003, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, DIR011, REL029, REL010, REL018, REL019, POS011, POS012]

Limitations: zero participation only means the old activities were not observed in the later window, so actual removal versus an simply unexercised path cannot be distinguished; the mixed pairwise orders show the absence of a fixed order, not that the five new activities run concurrently; and positions are event positions, not clock times. A complete shift in the mix of two coexisting process variants is a competing explanation that window-level evidence cannot rule out. [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL010]

Other differences: The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A44 and A45 roughly halved (mean about 1.0 → 0.5 hours; 157 vs 148 gaps). This is the only qualifying time item (1 against roughly 0.01 expected by chance in its family), so on its own it is the kind of result an unchanged process still produces occasionally, and no other evidence corroborates a timing change. [TWAIT001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

The evidence contains:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 163 units tested, 0.73 items expected without change. By family: control_flow: 144 units tested, 92 items, 0.72 expected; time: 19 units tested, 1 item, 0.009 expected.

So control flow family: 92 items vs 0.72 expected — massively many times larger than chance expectation. Time family: 1 item vs 0.009 expected — also much larger than chance (1 item when 0.009 expected is ~100x, though small counts; but the instruction says "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence'". Hmm, wait — for the time family, 1 item when 0.009 expected... The instruction says a count of the same order as that expectation (e.g., one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces. So for the time family, 1 item vs 0.009 expected — that's actually more than 100x the expectation. Hmm, but the example says "one or two items when fewer than one is expected" is what an unchanged process typically produces. That's a bit contradictory: 1 item when 0.009 expected is technically "many times larger". But the example explicitly says one or two items when fewer than one is expected is typical of an unchanged process. Hmm, let me re-read.

"A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks."

So for the time family: 1 item, expectation 0.009. One item when fewer than one is expected — per the example, this is what an unchanged process typically produces. So the single TWAIT item alone would be insufficient. But the control flow family has 92 items vs 0.72 expected — that's over 100x, clearly not explainable by chance.

"A count many times larger cannot be explained by chance as a whole, even when all items describe one underlying difference; do not merge items for this comparison."

So control flow: 92 items vs 0.72 expected → clearly a change. So we're past the screening gate. Now judge by directness, consistency, ability to rule out competing explanations.

Now let's understand the behavioural pattern.

Activities involved:
- A14, A17, A18, A19, A20: present in before (participation 0.165, 0.245, 0.265, 0.135, 0.19 respectively), absent in after (0.0).
- A15, A16, A25, A26, A27: absent in before, present in after with participation 1.0 (every trace), mean occurrences 1.0 per trace.
- A28: present in both windows (support 1.0 in both, per POS011: support 1.0 before and after). Its position shifted later: mean position 0.392 → 0.467.
- A43: present in both windows (support 1.0). Its position shifted earlier: mean 0.324 → 0.287.

DIR evidence:
- Before: A14→A28 (all of A14's outgoing goes to A28), A17→A28, A18→A28, A19→A28, A20→A28. So in the before window, A14, A17, A18, A19, A20 each had their only observed outgoing transition to A28.
- After: A15→{A25, A28, A27, A26, A16}, A16→{A27, A26, A15, A25, A28}, A25→{A16, A15, A27, A26, A28}, A26→{A28, A25, A16, A15, A27}, A27→{A26, A16, A28, A15, A25}. So in the after window, A15, A16, A25, A26, A27 form a densely connected block, each with outgoing transitions to the other four plus A28.
- DIR011: A43's outgoing redistributed: before A43→{A17: 0.245, A14: 0.165, A18: 0.265, A20: 0.19, A19: 0.135} (sums to 1.0), after A43→{A15: 0.25, A27: 0.195, A26: 0.205, A16: 0.18, A25: 0.17} (sums to 1.0). So A43 precedes the block: before it led into {A14, A17, A18, A19, A20}, after it leads into {A15, A16, A25, A26, A27}.

POS evidence:
- Before: A14 at mean position ~0.354, A17 ~0.355, A18 ~0.352, A19 ~0.365, A20 ~0.370. After: A15 ~0.372, A16 ~0.378, A25 ~0.383, A26 ~0.378, A27 ~0.375. So the new block sits at roughly the same relative position (~0.37-0.38 of the trace) as the old block (~0.35-0.37).
- A28: position shifted from ~0.392 to ~0.467 (later).
- A43: position shifted from ~0.324 to ~0.287 (earlier).

REL evidence:
- Before: A14 co-occurs with A28 in 16.5% of traces (A_only 0.165, i.e., A14 present without A28? wait). Let me re-read REL001: pair (A14, A15). Before: A_only 0.165 (A14 present, A15 absent), neither 0.835. After: B_only 1.0 (A15 present, A14 absent). So A14 and A15 never co-occur.

- REL057 (A26, A43): A43 before A26 always.
- REL058 (A27, A28): A27 before A28 always.
- REL059 (A27, A43): A43 before A27 always.
- REL011-014 (A15 vs A17/A18/A19/A20): before B_only (A17 etc. present without A15); after A_only 1.0 (A15 present, A17 absent). So old activities gone, new ones present.
- REL020-023 (A16 vs A17-A20): same pattern.
- REL032-034 (A17 vs A25/A26/A27): before A_only (A17 present, new ones absent); after B_only (new ones present, A17 absent).

- REL029-031, 037-038, 044: among A17-A20 pairs, before they were mutually exclusive alternatives (cooccurrence 0, A_only and B_only shares, neither ~0.5-0.68); after neither 1.0.

So the picture:

Before window: A43 occurs in every trace at relative position ~0.32, followed by exactly one of {A14, A17, A18, A19, A20} (mutually exclusive alternatives, participation 13.5%-26.5%, summing to 0.165+0.245+0.265+0.135+0.19 = 1.0), each of which leads to A28, which occurs in every trace at position ~0.39.

After window: A43 occurs in every trace at position ~0.29, followed by all five of {A15, A16, A25, A26, A27} (each in 100% of traces, once per trace, in mixed/unfixed order among themselves — each pair appears in both orders in roughly equal shares), all before A28, which occurs in every trace at position ~0.47.

So the change: a block of five mutually exclusive alternative activities (one chosen per case) was replaced by a block of five activities that all execute in every case in no fixed order between them. Also A43 moved slightly earlier and A28 later, consistent with the block growing from one activity to five.

Wait — is it "replaced"? The old activities A14, A17-A20 are absent in the after window; the new ones A15, A16, A25-A27 are absent in the before window. So it's a replacement of one set of activities by another set. This is not a "shift in path frequencies between existing alternatives" — the activities themselves changed. Per the guidance: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows" — not the case here. This is activities added/removed: the old alternatives disappeared and new activities appeared.

So the main hypothesis: the structure around A43 and A28 changed. Before, exactly one of five alternative activities (A14, A17, A18, A19, A20) executed between A43 and A28; after, five new activities (A15, A16, A25, A26, A27) all execute in every trace between A43 and A28, in no fixed order among themselves. A43 now sits slightly earlier and A28 slightly later in the trace, consistent with a longer block between them.

Support level: The screening comparison: control flow 92 items vs 0.72 expected — many times larger. Time family: 1 item vs 0.009 expected. Per the rule, one item when fewer than one is expected is what an unchanged process typically produces — so the TWAIT item alone would be insufficient. But the control-flow count is decisive.
